label: Grand Prix
insights: Max Verstappen won from P1 on S→M (1 stop).
Biggest climber: PIA, P17 to P3.
Best tyre management on Mediums: LEC, +0.012 s/lap over 12 laps.

allegation: Leaving the Track and Gaining an Advantage
detail: Moved into the path of a much faster car at Turn 17 while weaving
Changed direction under braking at Turn 14
Weaving on the entry to Turn 17
notes: Weaving to warm tyres; mitigated by an engine issue limiting energy deployment
Radio communication failure during the release
Left the track at Turn 8 while defending and did not give the position back
10 second penalty converted to a 5-place grid drop at the next race as he retired
Slowed under the Safety Car to create a gap for a double-stack pit stop

text: Floor Furniture Performance - Flow Conditioning New Board and Floor Edge A new floor board has been designed in conjunction with floor edge and diffuser, aiming at improved flow conditioning and aerodynamic load.

Floor Furniture Performance - Flow Conditioning Modified Rear Floor Furniture A small modification to the rear floor furniture, manipulating rear corner and diffuser flow with the aim of increasing aerodynamic efficiency.

Rear Wing  Circuit specific - Drag Range Various winglet devices removed from rear wing  Removing the rear wing winglets reduces assembly camber shedding local downforce and drag at a ratio appropriate for Vegas L/D.
Front Bodywork Circuit specific - Drag Range Mirror rear stay trim  The mirror stay trim reduces local camber and loading, shedding local downforce and drag at a ratio appropriate for Vegas L/D.

Rear Corner Performance - Local Load Rear corner winglets position and span Rear corner winglets position and span optimised around local load requirements, shedding local downforce and drag at a ratio appropriate for Vegas L/D.
Engine Cover Cooling Range Narrower rear exit A narrower rear exit allows more cooling range, appropriate for the lower cooling requirements of Vegas.

Front Wing Endplate Performance - Local Load Re-positioned Front Wing Endplate Dive-plane In order to better protect the flow stability of the front wing endplate footplate as well as surfaces downstream, the dive-plane has been lowered and reduced in chord length.

Floor Board Circuit specific - Drag Range Front floor board elements optimisation, single vertical element The primary aim of these modifications has been to adapt to Las Vegas circuit peculiar characteristics and car aerodynamic efficiency requirements. It is targeting aerodynamic drag saving, coming along with downforce reduction as a natural consequence, but in a favourable ratio for this track.

Floor Board   Circuit specific - Drag Range Shorter chord board elements A reduction in the amount of load generated by the Floor Board provides an improvement in overall efficiency and lap time around this circuit.

Rear Corner Circuit specific - Drag Range Modifications to drum winglets An alternative winglet arrangement on the rear brake drums delivers an efficient load reduction, providing a net performance benefit at this track.

Front Wing Circuit specific - Balance Range Reduced chord & incidence flap A low-balance front wing flap, featuring chord and incidence changes, is available for this circuit to reduce the load generated by the front wing and extend the available balance range.

Rear Wing Performance - Drag reduction Revised rear wing arrangement associated with the Straight Mode mechanism The revised arrangement is intended to evaluate an alternative rear wing Straight Mode deployment, with associated minor changes to accommodate the different configuration.

Rear Corner Circuit Specific – Drag Range  Updated rear brake duct deflector The revised rear brake duct deflector geometry was modified to match the specific aerodynamic efficiency requirements of the Las Vegas track.
